NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This is the second, deliberately small successor in the mint-baseline lineage. `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-1-5202CCD1` first drafted three removals at once; it was superseded into a narrow slice. `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-2-C2E3D3A3` implemented that slice: it removed the permanent historical mint regression from `src/grace-generate.test.ts` (the `BASE_COMMIT` constant `6dd1d95` and the detached-worktree test), retitled the depth assertion in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts`, and regenerated `test-metrics.json`. C-2 then reached final execution validation after the authority interpreted an earlier standalone `approved` as ratification of its spec. The maintainer later stated he had **not** approved that spec. Its approval records carry fingerprints matching the artifact bytes, but those records do not establish what the maintainer ratified. No apply or archive-close action ran; the maintainer directed a supersede. The verb discarded the bundle's governance, never its code, so the three product edits remain on the branch.
`C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-3-F04434E4` is the replacement named by that supersede. Its job is to attach valid governance to the already-present work without rewriting it. The adopted state is already the target state, so execution means **verify and close, not build**: the plan's `BaselineAssertions` describe the tree as it is now, an already-green target is acceptable, and no production file is reverted to manufacture a red. This re-ratification follows the archived `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2`, which re-ratified already-present citation-anchor work; that bundle declared `<None />` in `ObservedWriteScope`, and C-3 differs there by declaring this bundle's own archive arrival (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-3-F04434E4/**`) so the close's write is in scope under the current plan rule, while its production write surface is equally empty.
The retained tests are the discrimination the lineage keeps. The `spec new` race test and the implicit-supersede test drive the real `ngrace spec new` and `ngrace supersede` verbs against a disposable project; the two exported-route tests spawn Bun runners that import `mintResolvedBundle` and `mintBundle` directly. In every case the spawned process runs under an isolated-process preload that patches `node:fs.mkdirSync`, plants a competitor `spec.xml` and an unrelated file at the creation boundary **inside that process**, and reports that it fired on stderr. The repaired engine acquires the candidate leaf with a non-recursive `mkdir` whose `EEXIST` refuses, so the competitor survives byte-for-byte. Because each test asserts the planted competitor and the non-zero refusal, a green is not vacuous even without the permanent ancestor checkout.
The predecessor's one-time two-part red control is recorded here as lineage evidence, not as a requirement of this bundle. It was measured 2026-09-28 UTC on a copy of the repository at base `80cc36f789dc35ef789cfe6d753a39e7115dce76` with `node_modules` symlinked and no `.git`:
- baseline, restored file: `bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE: the repaired tree refuses"` exits 0, 1 pass. - mutation A (only the recursive `mkdir`: `mkdirSync(bundlePath, { recursive: true })`): the same command still exits 0, because the shipped `flag: "wx"` exclusive `spec.xml` write still refuses the existing competitor. Half the defect is masked; the red control must drive both halves. - mutation B (recursive `mkdir` together with the non-exclusive `writeFileSync(candidate.specPath, candidate.expectedSpecBytes)`): the same command exits 1 at `expect(result.exit, "the repaired leaf mkdir refuses").not.toBe(0)`, `Expected: not 0`. - restore: `cp` of the saved `src/grace-generate.ts` is byte-identical to the canonical file, and the same command exits 0 again.
During C-3 draft authoring (2026-09-28 UTC) mutation B was driven once on a disposable `git archive HEAD` copy at base `ac0013fa41aed0b94bba473a9e8113bae7428805` and restored byte-identical. That draft-time measurement is historical evidence only — not a task and not a `CloseEvidence` criterion — and no production file was reverted. The later bundle re-verifies the standing green on the real tree (four `AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE` tests pass) and does not itself run the mutation. The mutation is not in the suite and `src/grace-generate.test.ts` gains no planted-defect test.
The depth assertion stays because the declaration-count guard stays. `coverageRegressions` (`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:346`) reads `git show 2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2:<path>` for every existing `*.test.ts`, so the `validate` job must keep `fetch-depth: 0` and `validateJobCheckoutDepth` must keep asserting it. Carried `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY` (`C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-6-62765C22:712-729`) tied `fetch-depth: 0` to the `6dd1d95` control. This lineage overturns that historical-control **purpose clause** — the control is absent — while **retaining** `fetch-depth: 0` and the guard for the count guard's base; the later sequential bundle retires the remaining full-depth mechanism. Only the assertion's test title was untrue after the `6dd1d95` control is gone — it named the pinned baseline control as the reason — so the title is `the validate job checks out full history for the declaration-count coverage guard's historical base`. Every other symbol in the file, including `COVERAGE_BASE`, `declaredTests`, `coverageRegressions`, `collectTestFiles`, the coverage test, and the `validate:ci` one-suite-run guard, is retained.
`test-metrics.json` is **not** regenerated. `artifactIsStale` does not notice a deletion or a rename inside an existing test file, and this bundle writes no test file, so the artifact is fresh at base: 2455 cases across 69 files, the `tests` count equals the sum of the per-file counts, the retired mint test name and the old depth title are absent, and the new depth title is present. The plan asserts that relation; it does not re-emit the artifact.

Alternatives.Alternative: Re-run the predecessor's work from a pre-removal base (revert the three product files, then re-remove, re-retitle, and re-regenerate). Rejected: the edits are already committed and the verb discards governance, never code; reverting to manufacture a red is a fabricated failure, and the re-ratification exists precisely to avoid rewriting the standing work.

Set the base to the pre-implementation commit `80cc36f` and treat the three edits as future writes. Rejected: the edits are already present at HEAD, so a byte-invariance criterion against `80cc36f` would be false by construction, and the spec would pretend the writes are absent.

Regenerate `test-metrics.json` to give the bundle a live write. Rejected: the artifact is already measured against the present population and the test-file list is unchanged; a regeneration would change only timings and the generated date, and the purpose is to carry the relation, not to occupy a task slot.

Treat the disputed C-2 approval as valid and simply close C-2. Rejected: the maintainer stated he did not approve that spec; the fingerprints prove byte identity, not consent. Calling it valid would repeat the failure the supersede exists to correct.

Fix the approval-provenance gap in this bundle (one-time codes, a writable-nowhere approval service, or a pilot amendment budget). Rejected: that is `RM-VERIFIED-APPROVAL` and `RM-PILOT-APPROVAL` scope, and the brief forbids widening this successor into verified approval, Sashimi, or PILOT.

Author a baseline that requires the pre-removal tree so the plan starts red. Rejected: it would describe a state the repository is not in and would read as real baseline breakage; an already-green target is the honest shape for a re-ratification.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The approval-provenance gap belongs to `RM-VERIFIED-APPROVAL`; the incident and its measured cost are recorded in `docs/plans/active/RM-PILOT-APPROVAL/review.md` §9. This bundle neither implements a verifiable-approval service nor treats a CLI fingerprint as proof of consent, and it does not edit that record.

The next sequential bundle after this close retires the declaration-count coverage guard, the retitled depth assertion, and `fetch-depth: 0` together, then regenerates metrics; its expected implementation paths are `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts`, `.github/workflows/validate.yml`, and `test-metrics.json`. It answers applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` and retires the remaining `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY` full-depth mechanism. This bundle neither mints nor authors it.

Measured executed-code coverage is deferred to a later, separate small bundle, with its rationale recorded in project-specific memory outside this repository. This bundle keeps the weak declaration-count guard and adds no coverage tooling.

Scenarios.Scenario: The human-ratification stop: the spec is written `status="draft"` and stops there. The implementation authority requests ratification of `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-3-F04434E4` at spec stage only after its own review, and only a sufficient phrase from the maintainer moves it to `approved`. No plan, approval gate, execute epoch, apply, or close runs before that phrase.

A post-implementation checkout at base with the historical mint worktree operation already gone: the retained `spec new` race test, the implicit-supersede CLI test, and the two exported-route runner tests refuse the interspersed competitor, preserve the competitor bytes, and spawn no `git worktree`. This says nothing about the declaration-count guard's history read: the guard still requires the full-history `validate` job with base `2434fd4…`, and if that base is absent it **fails open** — `git show` exits non-zero and `coverageRegressions` `continue`s — so an absent-base green is a fail-open result, never evidence that the guard checked declarations.

The metric refresh relation: the committed `test-metrics.json` is fresh at base, names the new depth title and neither the retired mint test name nor the old depth title, lists every `.test.ts` under `src/` and `scripts/`, and its `tests` count equals the sum of the per-file counts. No regeneration is performed.

A post-close applied-archive tree: the historical mint test and `BASE_COMMIT` are absent, the depth assertion is retitled and passing, `.github/workflows/validate.yml` is byte-identical at the base, the declaration-count guard is intact and green under full history, lint is 0/0, and the narrow suites pass. The three adopted production paths are byte-identical to base.
